content.title: About
content.content: Cherries are the edible fruits of the sweet cherry tree (Prunus cerasus), native to temperate regions of the Northern Hemisphere. Raw cherries are bright red, have a tart‑sweet flavor and a juicy texture. They are eaten fresh, used in cooking, baking, desserts, and for making juices and preserves.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cherries belong to the Rosaceae family and are closely related to plums, apricots, and almonds.
There are over 400 cherry varieties, differing in taste, color, and harvest time.
Raw cherries are rich in antioxidants, especially anthocyanins, which give them their vivid red hue.
Cherry juice has been traditionally used in folk medicine to improve circulation.
Cherries were among the first fruits cultivated by the ancient Romans.

items.title: High in vitamin C
items.content: Cherries provide a substantial amount of vitamin C, which supports the immune system and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Anthocyanins and polyphenols in cherries help combat free radicals and may reduce the risk of chronic diseases.

items.title: Heart‑healthy
items.content: Potassium and fiber in cherries contribute to normal blood pressure and improve lipid profiles.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: Fiber promotes intestinal motility and helps maintain regular bowel movements.

items.title: Contains melatonin
items.content: Cherries naturally contain melatonin, a hormone that regulates sleep, which may support better rest.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to cherries, manifesting as skin rash or swelling.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Raw cherries contain natural sugars, so people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: The acidic nature of cherries can irritate the stomach lining in those with heightened sensitivity.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raw cherries can be enjoyed as a snack, added to oatmeal, yogurt, salads, baked goods, or used to make sauces and compotes. If desired, pits can be removed with specialized tools.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cherries in the refrigerator in an airtight container, where they stay fresh for 7‑10 days. For longer storage, freeze the berries in a single layer on a tray, then transfer to a freezer bag.
